content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an LLM agent. The printer chat panel lets the model add a printer and connect it with five tools: `printer_identify`, `printer_add`, `printer_change`, `printer_connection_status` and `printer_connect`. Bambu Lab printers are found by Orca's SSDP network search and connected in LAN mode with an access code; Moonraker and OctoPrint printers connect by a typed address.

On 2026-10-31 Kenneth tried to connect his own Bambu P1S (192.168.0.198) through the chat and never could. The app log `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/log/debug_Sat_Oct_31_07_19_33_85053.log.0` shows: `printer_connect` refused at 07:25:27 with "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now" although no network search had started; the search began only at 18:22:30 (first `printer_connection_status`); SSDP announced the P1S at 18:23:08 with `con_type= cloud, bind_state= occupied` (re-announcing about every 10 s); a second connect was refused at 18:23:15 with the same sentence. The model saw no difference between "no search yet", "search 0 s old" and "a P1S at the typed address, in cloud mode". Root cause: the app observed these states and reported none of them. The chat text was not saved and the model used is unknown, so the model's own mistake (asking for an address) is not in scope.

Constraints from Kenneth: the standing system prompt holds principles only; a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`; the app must never report a guess as fact or hide an error; other brands, people who rely on Bambu's cloud features, and people who do not want to connect must not be worse off; changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files need `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`, but all three bugs are in fork-owned `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/`. No live-model prompt run without Kenneth's approval. Developer Mode guidance text is out of scope until tested on the printer. Read `AGENTS.md` first (build on the shared Mac with `-j4`, one build per directory, check `pgrep -fl ninja` first). Temporary notes stay untracked.

Task:
Reproduce and fix three bugs in the printer chat's Bambu connection tools, all in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp` and the tool descriptions in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`. Write a failing Catch2 test for each bug first in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` using the existing `FakeBackend` fixtures (`bambu_on_network()` already includes a cloud-mode candidate `CLOUD01`), then fix, then run the agent tests and the AgentUI tests.

Bug 1, false refusal. `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` for `printer_connect` (the `unknown_device` branch, around line 388) says "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now" even when no search has run (`m_prepared` is empty for this printer). The message must not claim what the app has not checked: when no search has run, say so and name `printer_connection_status`.

Bug 2, hidden observations. `connection_json` (around line 120) drops every candidate with `lan_mode == false` before the model sees it, although `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection` in `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` already lists them with name, IP and mode. Report printers of this model that were seen but cannot be offered in the status result, each with name, address and a reason (cloud mode, meaning LAN Only is off), separate from the connectable LAN candidates. In the `printer_connect` refusal, when the model's argument names or matches a seen cloud-mode printer (by id, name or address), say that printer is on the network with LAN Only off. Put the reading rule in the tool descriptions: a cloud-mode entry means LAN Only is off on the printer, connecting is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection. The test at `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:955` asserts the current hiding; change it deliberately and say why in the commit. Extend `printer_connection_schema()` in `ToolRegistry.cpp` and `PrinterPanel.tsx` or `bridge/protocol.ts` only if the page renders the result.

Bug 3, empty first read. `connection_status` (around line 557) starts the search with `prepare_connection` and reads the list in the same call, so the first read is empty by construction. Return the search state in the result (not started, started N seconds ago, listening), and from `tick()` post a note through `m_host.post_note` plus `start_turn` when the first printer of this model appears, or after about 15 s with none, the same way the existing connection-outcome notes work. Keep the "start the search once" rule in the comment above `m_prepared`.

Verification: Catch2 agent tests green (`tests/agent`), AgentUI tests green (`npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`), the `tests/printer_prompt` fixtures (`run_prompt_tests.py` fakes `unknown_device` around line 813) updated to the new result shape without running the live model, and a no-model live check against the real P1S at 192.168.0.198 in cloud mode through the manual tool harness (see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`; the shell harness has a manual MCP mode where `probe.call` drives any tool) showing the status result names the P1s at that address as seen in cloud mode and the connect refusal says so. Do not run a live-model prompt batch; do not add Developer Mode guidance text. Done is a commit on the worktree branch with the tests, the fix, and the harness output quoted in an untracked note at the worktree root.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_05f541e9-abc1-4ee8-a987-a295f5fa2c65

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Throws and log lines may name Orca; they never reach the model.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

80	
81	- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
82	- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
83	- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
84	- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
85	- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
86	- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

88	## Critical Constraints
89	
90	- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
91	- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
92	- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
93	- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app
94	
95	## Code review focus areas
96	
97	- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
98	- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
99	- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
100	- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
101	- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
102	- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
103	- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
104	- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

1	# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)
2	
3	Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
4	Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
5	MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.
6	
7	The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
8	`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
9	fake unless asked.
10	
11	This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.
12	
13	## What success looks like
14	
15	- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
16	- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
17	- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
18	- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
19	  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.
20	
21	If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
22	fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.
23	
24	## Turn it on
25	
26	Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.
27	
28	`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:
29	
30	```json
31	"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
32	```
33	
34	JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
35	the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.
36	
37	Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
38	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
39	`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
40	either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
41	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
42	`orca`.
43	
44	**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
45	as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
46	Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
47	`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
48	`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
49	`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.
50	
51	Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
52	config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
53	lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
54	beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.
55	
56	The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
57	**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.
58	
59	For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
60	`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
61	**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
62	prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
63	fixture rewrites it at startup.
64	
65	## Drive state
66	
67	Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
68	fake rereads it about once a second.
69	
70	```json
71	{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
72	```
73	
74	| Field | Meaning |
75	|---|---|
76	| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
77	| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
78	| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
79	| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
80	| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |
81	| `send_fails` | `true` makes the next print or storage upload fail as an upload failure (read at the moment of Send), so OrcaSlicer's send dialog shows its error and reports no success |
82	
83	No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
84	field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
85	tray per spool, up to 4:
86	
87	```json
88	{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
89	```
90	
91	`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
92	when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
93	saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
94	spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
95	`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
96	`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
97	id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
98	draws no swatch for it.
99	
100	Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.
101	
102	## Print
103	
104	Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
105	The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.
106	
107	If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
108	menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
109	scenario after send.
110	
111	## Isolate a running app (agents)
112	
113	Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.
114	
115	On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
116	a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
117	`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
118	`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.
119	
120	Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
121	posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
122	half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
123	title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
124	for Print.
125	
126	Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
127	use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.
128	
129	## Unit tests
130	
131	`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
132	control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
133	test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.
134	
135	## Agent id
136	
137	Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
138	id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

2026-10-20, add-printer form harness check: three separate leftovers made later `--printer-setup` checks stall or fail, though the new checks all passed. A run with the new check removed passed, which is how the cause was proven to be leftover state, not a product bug.

3. A user filament preset left in slot 1 is a candidate for OrcaSlicer's "customized presets" load warning; restore slot 1 and delete copies the check made.

# Bambu connection fixes: what was checked, 2026-11-01

Temporary note, untracked. Three bugs in the printer chat's connection tools are fixed on branch
`claude/festive-lederberg-693438`. **The check against the real P1S has not been done**: the printer was not
answering on 2026-11-01 morning. Everything below it was run.

## Still to do: the real printer

The P1S's last announcement in Kenneth's app log is 2026-10-31 23:07, and TCP ports 8883 and 990 on 192.168.0.198
time out. Kenneth's running JusPrin (pid 85053) also held UDP 2021, the port printers announce on, and the harness
never bound it during its run. Whether that alone would hide the printer is not known.

Needs: the P1S on and in cloud mode, and that JusPrin quit. Then:

```bash
cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438
F=/tmp/claude/netcheck; rm -rf "$F"; mkdir -p "$F"
cp -R "$HOME/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/plugins" "$F/plugins"
build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-network-check "$F" 192.168.0.198 02.03.00.62 2>&1 | grep -aE "HARNESS (NETWORK|RESULT)|network_check.*FAIL"
```

It takes about a minute with the printer on, and sends the printer nothing.

## Why the harness is not the one the task named

`probe.call` cannot reach these tools. McpServer.cpp refuses them with "This tool is not exposed by JusPrin MCP.",
because they have only `ToolExposure::Printer`. So the commit adds `--printer-network-check`: no model, the real
plug-in, the real `OrcaPrinterBackend`, and a scripted stand-in for the model.

## Real plug-in, printer off (`HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=2`)

The two failures are the checks that need the printer. Quoted from the run:

```
printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> {"error":{"code":"unknown_device","message":"No network search has run yet in this conversation; printer_connection_status starts it."}}
printer_connection_status {} -> {"address":"","candidates":[],"hostType":"","message":"","nozzleMismatch":false,"provider":"bambu","search":{"secondsAgo":0,"state":"started"},"seen":[],"state":"not_configured"}
printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> {"error":{"code":"unknown_device","message":"The network search started 0 seconds ago and has found no printer of this model yet. The app posts a note when one appears, or after about 15 seconds with none."}}
note at 15 s: The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears.
printer_connection_status {} -> {"address":"","candidates":[],"hostType":"","message":"","nozzleMismatch":false,"provider":"bambu","search":{"secondsAgo":120,"state":"listening"},"seen":[],"state":"not_configured"}
```

## Simulated announcement (`HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`)

**No printer was involved.** With `--simulate-announce`, 25 seconds in, the harness hands
`DeviceManager::on_machine_alive` the announcement recorded in the 2026-10-31 log. This tests everything after the
plug-in, including `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection`, and not the plug-in itself. After the same first three lines:

```
note at 15 s: The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears.
simulated announcement, no printer involved
note at 25 s: The network search found P1s at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, which cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection.
printer_connection_status {} -> {"address":"","candidates":[],"hostType":"","message":"","nozzleMismatch":false,"provider":"bambu","search":{"secondsAgo":25,"state":"listening"},"seen":[{"address":"192.168.0.198","name":"P1s","reason":"cloud_mode"}],"state":"not_configured"}
printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> {"error":{"code":"unknown_device","message":"P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network with LAN Only off. It cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection."}}
printer_connect {"deviceId":"P1s"} -> the same refusal
printer_connect {"address":"192.168.0.198","hostType":"moonraker"} -> the same refusal
```

## Tests

- Before the fix: `[printer-conversation]` had 7 of 67 test cases failing, 46 assertions, with the old sentence

content.text:
The three bugs are fixed and committed as `ff2fee4fbd` on `claude/festive-lederberg-693438` (unmerged), with tests passing. The check against the real P1S is **not done**, so the printer-at-its-address result has only been shown with a simulated announcement.

## The real printer check
- **What happened:** the P1S was off at first. It came back around 07:22, but a real run at 07:23 still saw nothing in 120 seconds.
- **Likely cause (not verified):** your running JusPrin (pid 85053) holds UDP 2021, the port printers announce on, and the harness never bound it. I tried a packet capture to confirm this, but `tcpdump` was refused permission. macOS local network permission for the harness could also be the cause.
- **What did run on the real plug-in:** the first two refusals, the first status read and the 15-second note.
- **What was simulated:** I replayed the announcement from your 2026-10-31 log into the app, with no printer involved. That run passed:
  - The status result names `P1s` at 192.168.0.198 with reason `cloud_mode`.
  - `printer_connect` refuses by address, name or host-style address, saying: "P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network with LAN Only off."
  - This covers everything after the plug-in, but not the plug-in itself.

## What changed
- **False refusal:** `printer_connect` now says no search has run and names `printer_connection_status`, or says how long the search has been running.
- **Hidden printers:** the status result has a new `seen` list, separate from `candidates`, and the refusal names a seen printer when asked for it. The reading rule is in both tool descriptions.
- **Empty first read:** the result now carries `search.state`. The app posts a note and starts a model turn when the first printer appears, or after 15 seconds with none. A printer found later still gets a note, because the P1S took 38 seconds to answer on 10-31.

## Tests

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Printer conversation tests before the fix | 7 of 67 failed |
| Agent tests after the fix | all 497 pass |
| AgentUI tests | 624 pass |
| Shell harness `--printer-setup` | 252 checks pass |
| `test_responses.py` (no model) | 8 of 9 pass |

The one failure in `test_responses.py` isn't from this change: it searches `OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` for text that now lives in `ProviderAgent.cpp`. I left it alone. No live-model prompt was run.

## Where I went beyond or differed from the brief
- **Harness:** `probe.call` can't reach these tools, because MCP refuses them. I added `--printer-network-check`, which runs them with a scripted stand-in for the model.
- **Account-only printers:** `CLOUD01` has no address, and printers like it can come from your Bambu account list, wherever they physically are. Calling it "on the network with LAN Only off" would be a guess, so it gets its own reason, `account_only`.
- **Prompt edit:** "None listed means LAN mode is off" contradicted the search state, so I moved it from `printerInstructions.ts` into the status tool's description. No model has been tested with this wording.
- **Base branch:** the worktree started on `main`, which lacks this code, so I moved it to `jusprin-newui` before committing. It's based on the rewritten `69780c7af4`, whose only code difference from the old base I confirmed is that one test file.

## Remaining risks
- **Repeated polling:** after the 15-second note the app keeps looking every 5 seconds until a printer appears or the chat closes. Each look runs `saved_printers()` on the GUI thread, and I didn't measure the cost.
- **Extra reply:** if someone says "never mind" right after a status check, the 15-second note still makes the model reply once more.

The harness output and the exact command for the real run are in [printer-connect-live-check.md](printer-connect-live-check.md), which is untracked.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>Bash, Edit, Monitor, Read, ToolSearch, Write, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Original task (from the parent session `local_05f541e9-abc1-4ee8-a987-a295f5fa2c65`, relayed; my report goes back to it, with the first 400 characters relayed, so lead with what was done and the commit):** reproduce and fix three bugs in JusPrin's printer chat Bambu connection tools, failing Catch2 test first in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp`:
     - Bug 1: false refusal "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now" when no search has run; must say so and name `printer_connection_status`.
     - Bug 2: `connection_json` hid cloud-mode printers; report them separately with name, address, reason; refusal names a matching one by id, name or address; reading rule in tool descriptions (cloud-mode means LAN Only off, connecting is the person's choice, printer prepares prints without a connection); deliberately change test at old line 955 and say why in the commit.
     - Bug 3: first read empty; return search state; from `tick()` post a note + `start_turn` when first printer appears or after ~15 s with none; keep the "start the search once" rule in the comment above `m_prepared`.
     - Verification: agent tests, AgentUI `npm test`, `tests/printer_prompt` fixtures updated without running live model, no-model live check against real P1S at 192.168.0.198 in cloud mode; commit on worktree branch; harness output quoted in an untracked note at the worktree root.
     - **This is complete: commit `ff2fee4fbd`, real P1S check passed.**
   - **Current request from the user ("Yes, add it here"; the button's meaning: "Detect that another app holds UDP 2021 and report it in the search result and the note, with a failing test first."):** the app should detect that UDP 2021 is taken and say so in the search result and note. In progress and uncommitted.
   - **Standing constraints (preserve):**
     - Standing system prompt holds principles only; a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description in `ToolRegistry.cpp`. The app must never report a guess as fact or hide an error. Other brands, people relying on Bambu's cloud features, and people who do not want to connect must not be worse off. Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files need `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` (all work so far is in fork-owned `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and tests). **No live-model prompt run without Kenneth's approval.** Developer Mode guidance text is out of scope until tested on the printer; do not add it. Temporary notes stay untracked, never committed and never hidden via `.gitignore`/`.git/info/exclude`.
     - AGENTS.md: shared Mac: `-j4`, one build per build dir, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, never restart a build to change targets; wording the model reads says "the app", never Orca; files are "opened/imported/loaded/added", never "arrived"; error-handling discipline; cross-platform requirement.
     - Global CLAUDE.md: git commits allowed without confirmation when confident after reviewing `git status`/`git diff`; **revert/amend/reset and any history-modifying operation requires explaining and explicit user confirmation**; never commit submodule updates; never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce; test changes end to end; label inference vs verified fact; use service account for gcloud/kubectl. Do not add attribution lines to commit messages or PR bodies. Do not use bare `git stash` (shared stack). Never `git checkout <file>` to undo temp edits (use a copy). Output style Plain: cold-reader summaries, open with 2–3 understandable sentences; they/them when pronouns unknown. Do not push or open a PR unless asked.
     - Only the printer is listened to; nothing is sent to it. Don't drive or quit Kenneth's own JusPrin myself.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - OrcaSlicer fork (C++17, wxWidgets, Catch2 v3), `PrinterConversation` (GUI-free, tested with `FakeBackend` + `RecordingPanel`), `IPrinterBackend`/`OrcaPrinterBackend`, `IConversationHost::post_note/start_turn`, `tick()` pump from `PrinterPanel`.
   - Bambu SSDP discovery: printers announce to UDP 2021 (source port 1900); plug-in `libbambu_networking_02.03.00.62.dylib`; `DeviceManager::on_machine_alive`, `localMachineList` (announced on network; cloud-mode entries come only from SSDP) vs `userMachineList` (account, printers may be anywhere; stale `ip_address` possible).
   - `is_lan_mode_printer()` = `dev_connection_type == "lan"`. Discovery is stopped only at plug-in reload and app exit (GUI_App.cpp:1757, 2597); started at GUI_App.cpp:998, 1623 and `prepare_connection`.
   - Printer tools have only `ToolExposure::Printer`, so MCP refuses them ("This tool is not exposed by JusPrin MCP."); `probe.call` cannot reach them.
   - `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[printer]'` regenerates `tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json`.
   - Fail-first guard proof: remove a part of the fix, see tests fail, restore from a copy.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   Worktree: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`, branch `claude/festive-lederberg-693438`, HEAD `ff2fee4fbd` on base `69780c7af4` (local `jusprin-newui`, rewritten; only code difference from old base `dc3cffe1fc` is 3 lines in `MessageList.scroll.test.tsx`, verified). Build dir `build/arm64`, **config Release**.
   
   Committed in `ff2fee4fbd`:
   - `PrinterConversation.cpp/.hpp`: `kSearchWait`=15 s, `kSearchLateLook`=5 s, `kPersonsChoice`, helpers `with_address`, `found_on_network`, `not_offered_text`, `connection_json(info, search)`, members `unknown_device_text`, `search_text`, `search_json`, `watch_search`; `m_search` (`std::optional<NetworkSearch>`), reset in `start()`, `install_network_plugin`, `undo_add`, and when `m_prepared != name`. Status result has `seen` [{name,address,reason: cloud_mode|account_only}] and `search` {state, secondsAgo}. A printer already `verified` sets `found` so no notes.
   - `PrinterBackend.hpp`: `ConnectionCandidate::account_only`. `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection`: `nearby = get_local_machinelist()`; `account_only = nearby.find(id) == nearby.end()`.
   - `ToolRegistry.cpp`: `printer_connection_schema()` plus both descriptions. `printerInstructions.ts`: removed "None listed…" sentence (moved to status description). `run_prompt_tests.py` fixtures and `printer_tools.json`. `Testing/README.md` section "A real printer, no model". `shell_harness.cpp`: `--printer-network-check <dir> <address> <plugin-version> [--simulate-announce]`, `verify_printer_network_check`, `network_check_call`; harness gives up waiting at 120 s.

   Uncommitted now (all from the port work; `git status` shows these modified):
   - `PrinterBackend.hpp`:
     ```cpp
     // Who holds the UDP port Bambu Lab printers announce themselves on. Discovery
     // reports success even when another program holds it, and hears nothing.
     enum class DiscoveryPort { Ours, Taken, Free };
     ...

input.recap: Commit ff10faa501 makes the printer chat report when it cannot hear Bambu printers on UDP 2021. Real P1S runs behaved correctly with the port free, held and let go. Windows reports nothing, Linux wasn't run, nothing is pushed, and recovery needs an app restart.

content.text:
Commit `ff10faa501` on `claude/festive-lederberg-693438` makes the printer chat say when it can't hear Bambu printers because UDP port 2021 isn't available to it. Before this, it reported that it had listened and found nothing, which suggested the printer was off or in the wrong mode. The app can't recover by itself, so the message asks the person to restart it; nothing is pushed.

**What the app does now:** if the search has found nothing after 15 seconds, the app checks who holds the port. The check gives one of two new values for `search.state` in the `printer_connection_status` result, and a matching note goes to the model and starts a turn:
- **`port_taken`:** another app holds the port, so the person needs to close that app and then restart this one.
- **`not_listening`:** nothing holds the port and this app doesn't have it either, so the person needs to restart this app.

**Why a restart:** the Bambu plug-in binds the port only as the app starts. After the other program let go, the port stayed empty with each of these:
- stopping and starting discovery
- doing that with a wait in between
- doing that with the plug-in's "sending" flag set as well
- reloading the plug-in

My first version promised the search would start again by itself. A live run showed that was false, so I removed it.

**Real P1S runs, with a Python script holding the port:**

| Port | Result |
|---|---|
| Free | Printer found at 14 s, no port note, `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0` |
| Held throughout | Port note at 15 s, status `port_taken` at 120 s |
| Let go after the first note | Second note at 20 s, status `not_listening` at 120 s |

The last two runs end in `HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=2`, which is expected because those two checks need the printer to be heard.

**Other tests, all rerun with this code unless noted:**
- **Agent tests:** all pass, 20126 assertions in 499 test cases. The new port tests failed before the change, as they should.
- **AgentUI `npm test`:** 624 passed.
- **Fake-printer harness (`--printer-setup`):** passes.
- **`tests/printer_prompt/test_responses.py`:** 8 of 9 pass. The failure is `test_the_unrun_result_is_the_apps_own`, the same one as before this work, because it searches a file the text has since moved out of. I didn't fix it.
- **Live model:** no prompt run, so how the model responds to the new notes and wording is unmeasured.

**Limits:**
- **Windows:** it makes no claim, and whether a held port hides printers there is untested.
- **Linux:** the code path has not been run.
- **Other slicers:** only another JusPrin and the Python script have held the port, not Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer.
- **Test coverage:** the agent tests use a fake for the port, so only the live runs exercise the real socket check.

The quoted harness output and these limits are in `printer-connect-live-check.md` at the worktree root, untracked as you asked.
Have you reproduced these bugs before you fixed them? What's the status in plain English under a hundred words?

Partly. I reproduced the three chat bugs only as failing tests with a fake printer backend, not in the real app; I ran the real P1S only after those fixes. I did reproduce the port problem on the real P1S before fixing it: nothing was found in 120 seconds while another app held the port.

Status: both commits (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) are on the branch, unpushed, and the real-printer checks behave correctly. Windows and Linux are unverified, and no live-model run has happened.
Make sure you reproduce all three using the real app. I don't want to you fix the bugs that are in imagination only

I'll put the old code back temporarily, keeping only the harness, and run it against the real P1S to see which of the three bugs actually show up. First I'm checking what the harness needs from the old code, whether the port is free, and whether your real app's logs already show the bugs.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Listens on UDP 2021 only; sends nothing. Prints each distinct announcement
# from the printer with the fields that say which mode it is in.
import re, socket, sys, time

seconds = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 60
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(("", 2021))
s.settimeout(1)
start = time.time()
seen = 0
last = None
while time.time() - start < seconds:
    try:
        data, addr = s.recvfrom(4096)
    except socket.timeout:
        continue
    seen += 1
    text = data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    fields = dict(re.findall(r"^([A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+):\s*(.*?)\r?$", text, re.M))
    summary = {k: v for k, v in fields.items() if "bbl" in k.lower() or k.lower() in ("location", "usn")}
    if summary != last:
        print(f"{time.time()-start:5.1f}s from {addr[0]}: {summary}", flush=True)
        last = summary
print(f"{seen} announcements in {seconds}s", flush=True)

**Yes, I need one thing from you: turn on LAN Only on the P1S.** As of 18:28 it's still announcing cloud mode, and that's the only thing holding up the last test. If you'd rather not, tell me and I'll stop and put the code back.

**Where this started:** on 2026-10-31 you tried to connect your P1S in the printer chat, and the app wrongly said no printer was there. The session that started this one asked me to fix three bugs in the Bambu connection tools:
1. The app says "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now" even when no search has run yet.
2. It hides printers in cloud mode, so the model can't tell the person the printer was found but needs LAN Only turned on.
3. The first read comes back empty, and nothing tells the model when a printer shows up later.

**What I've done:**

On the P1S, LAN Only mode is set from the printer screen, and the access code shows up in the same menu.

**Steps on the printer:**
- Open Settings (the gear icon) and select WLAN. LAN Only Mode is listed there, and it starts out switched off.
- Turn the switch on and confirm when prompted. The option changes to "ON" once the switch has taken effect.
- Write down the access code. It sits directly under the LAN Only switch.

**Binding in Bambu Studio:** Open the printer list popup under the Device page, find the printer that has been switched to LAN-only mode, then enter the access code and click "Confirm." If discovery fails, choose Device > No Printer > Bind with Access Code.

**Troubleshooting:**
- If the access code shows all zeros, press the refresh icon next to it, or temporarily toggle LAN Only mode off and on. The code keeps working after you turn LAN Only off again.
- Developer Mode is a separate toggle that builds on LAN Only mode, so LAN Only has to be enabled first.
- Some users report binding problems in LAN Only mode, especially with network or 5GHz settings. One forum thread describes deactivating 5GHz and power cycling the printer, but the thread does not confirm that as a fix.

Menu labels can vary by firmware version, so check the wiki if the screen differs.
